title: Security posture discovery with Elysian Bio
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzales (Elysian Bio - MLOps), Tom Reed (Elysian - Security), Leah Park (Elysian - Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Elysian discussed security posture requirements for potential Redwood deployment. Main topics: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML and SSO integrations, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS (BYOK options), and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Action items: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs and pen test summary; schedule technical deep dive for VPC/KMS and provide benchmark checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya, our SE. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Maria Gonzales: Good, thanks. We've got Tom and Leah on as well. We're mostly here to walk through security questions before we can go talk to procurement.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Great. Maybe we can start with your main concerns, Maria? What would make you comfortable with Hosted vs Dedicated or Private?
[00:24] Maria: Sure. The shortlist is SOC2 / ISO27001, SSO / SAML integration with Okta, RBAC (least privilege) for our teams, strong audit logs with long retention for regulated projects, and customer-managed keys ideally. Also data residency - some workloads need EU only.
[00:39] Tom Reed: Also we do annual pen tests and need to know how you surface those results; and we need explicit SLA language around data deletion and retention.
[00:46] Alex: Totally, that makes sense. Quick high level: Redwood Hosted is our fastest path, SOC2 Type II is available, we also have ISO certification in progress — um, Priya can add details — Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and VPC peering, and Private deployment gives a customer-controlled control plane + on-prem option for air-gapped.
[01:08] Priya: Yeah, SOC2 Type II report we can share under NDA. ISO27001 we achieved last year, I believe we have the cert and scope doc — we'll include that. For pen tests we have an annual third-party engagement; we can share the summary and remediation notes.
[01:27] Maria: Okay, good. On keys — are you offering BYOK (bring your own key) for KMS? We can't have provider-managed keys for certain PHI-like workloads.
[01:36] Priya: For Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via a KMS integration in some regions; there are some limitations on cross-region failover with BYOK but we can go into specifics in the tech deep dive. Dedicated and Private both support BYOK and HSM integrations as part of the private control plane.
[01:52] Leah Park: When you say KMS integration, is that with AWS KMS only or do you support Azure Key Vault or GCP KMS?
[01:59] Priya: We support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault today; GCP KMS support is planned and in beta with a few partners. We'll document the exact versions and permissions model.
[02:09] Tom: How are audit logs handled? We need immutable logs for access and admin actions, retained for at least 2 years for some workflows.
[02:18] Alex: Good question. We capture admin actions, API access, model routing, and infra events. For Hosted we retain logs for 90 days by default, with options for extended retention as a paid add-on — we can export to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to a customer S3/GCS bucket. For Dedicated and Private you can set retention to meet your policy, and you control export destinations.
[02:41] Maria: S3 export sounds fine but we need proof the logs are tamper-evident. Do you do signed log delivery or append-only storage?
[02:49] Priya: We can enable write-once object locks on S3 exports and include delivery checksums; for Private there's more direct control, and we can also support forwarding to your WORM storage. We'll add specifics to the security packet.
[03:02] Alex: Also want to flag data-in-transit and at-rest encryption standards — TLS1.2+ in flight, at-rest AES-256 for model artifacts and KV cache, though sometimes the transcription shows K-V cash — sorry, that was a bad phrase — but basically AES-256.
[03:18] Maria: Speaking of the KV cache — we store some prefixes in cache; is that considered persisted data? How is it cleared on deprovision or model change?
[03:26] Priya: KV cache is persisted on disk for performance on serving nodes; for Hosted it's handled by our runtime with configurable TTLs, and for Dedicated/Private you can configure TTLs and eviction policies and we can do full cache flush during decommissions. We'll document the lifecycle and provide an API for explicit cache clears.
[03:44] Tom: For SSO we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning; we need RBAC mapping to Okta groups so we can do least privilege.
[03:53] Alex: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC in the console supports role templates and custom roles; we map to external groups and you can limit admin-level permissions. For Hosted we support SSO + SCIM; Dedicated + Private allow network-restricted SSO endpoints if you want.
[04:12] Leah: Is there session logging per user for actions like model version promotions and key rotations?
[04:18] Priya: Yes, audit logs include user-level actions including model rollouts, key rotations, and changes to routing policies. Again exports available to SIEM; timestamps approximately synced to NTP.
[04:28] Maria: About data deletion — if we ask for data to be deleted, what's the SLA? We need proof that tokens and inputs are removed across caches, logs, and backups.
[04:37] Alex: We have a documented data deletion workflow. For Hosted, typical deletion propagation is up to 7 days for caches and 30 days for backups, though we can put hard SLAs in enterprise contracts. For Dedicated/Private you get faster control and we can agree to shorter windows. We'll include the deletion spec in the packet.
[04:54] Tom: Are you doing encryption at rest on backups? We want backups encrypted with customer-managed keys where possible.
[05:00] Priya: Yes, backups are encrypted; BYOK for backups is supported on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys in supported regions — we'll share the matrix.
[05:10] Alex: There was a question earlier about ISO — we are ISO27001 certified, scope includes platform and operations — Priya?
[05:18] Priya: We completed ISO27001 last quarter; we'll include certificate and statement of applicability. Also include our risk register high-level items that are shareable.
[05:28] Maria: Good. Pen test: can you provide remediation timelines and do you allow an attestation of fixes?
[05:34] Priya: We share an executive summary and remediation plan; for enterprise customers we can share a redacted report and provide an attestation that issues affecting the environment have been resolved.
[05:44] Tom: For on-prem/private, how does the control plane work? We want to maintain network isolation and control of keys and logs.
[05:51] Alex: Private deployment gives you a customer-managed control plane; the data plane can be air-gapped on-prem. You manage the control plane credentials, networking. For dedicated we can do VPC peering and customer-managed subnets, but the control plane remains Redwood-managed in a private tenancy — different tradeoffs.
[06:10] Leah: What about upgrade processes? We run strict change windows; how are upgrades to the runtime handled?
[06:16] Priya: For Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows and keep you on pinned runtime versions if needed; for Private you manage upgrades, but we provide upgrade artifacts and a checklist.
[06:25] Maria: One more: regulatory proofs — we sometimes need to show auditors where the keys are and the key rotation schedule. Can you provide rotation logs?
[06:33] Priya: Yes, KMS rotation events are in the audit logs and we can provide rotation policy docs.
[06:39] Alex: Quick clarification: when folks ask about "model outputs" and PHI, we recommend using Private or Dedicated for strict isolation. Hosted is possible if you configure data routing and BYOK, but some customers prefer Dedicated for more guarantees.
[06:53] Maria: Understood. Cost tradeoffs come in but compliance wins here.
[06:57] Tom: A few nitty-gritty items: 1) Are you SOC2 Type II only or also have PCI scope? 2) Do you support pen test evidence sharing under NDA? 3) Is there a SOC2 description / system boundaries doc?
[07:12] Priya: SOC2 Type II report is available; we do not claim PCI scope unless specifically contracted with the relevant attestation. We can share the SOC2 description and system boundaries under NDA, yes.
[07:22] Maria: For retention, some of our projects require 3 years; is that doable?
[07:26] Alex: For Hosted, extended retention to multi-year is possible via archive export to your storage — there's a cost. For Dedicated/Private you'll have full control and can meet the 3-year requirement.
[07:36] Leah: About log immutability — can you support chain-of-custody requests?
[07:40] Priya: We can provide signed delivery and object locking. For Private you can leverage your own custody tooling.
[07:46] Tom: Do you offer CSPM / continuous compliance checks or integrations to our existing tools?
[07:50] Alex: We integrate with a few posture tools and can provide config exports; we also provide an ops checklist for security scanning.
[07:58] Maria: Let's talk timeline: procurement wants to close next quarter if security checks out. We may need a pilot on Dedicated for a particular model workload.
[08:07] Alex: That sounds reasonable. Typical next steps would be to share security artifacts, then schedule a SE-led technical deep dive that includes VPC and KMS demos and maybe run a small benchmark.
[08:19] Priya: For the tech deep dive we'll want sample throughput numbers and the expected sequence lengths for token estimates; that helps with quantization recommendations and batching.
[08:29] Maria: We'll share sample throughput and retention constraints.
[08:32] Tom: One more — do you have SOC audit logs that show who accessed which logs? We need to correlate user actions to logs.
[08:40] Priya: Yes, audit events include the user id and the action; we can correlate IDP user principal to actions for SSO flows.
[08:46] Alex: We're getting close to time — want to recap?
[08:49] Maria: Sure. Recap items: Redwood to send SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs, pen test summary, KMS BYOK docs including region support matrix, audit log export options and immutability controls, and data deletion SLA. We'll review and then schedule the technical deep dive.
[09:07] Priya: Action items noted. Any objections or other items?
[09:11] Leah: None from me.
[09:12] Tom: No.
[09:13] Alex: Great. We'll email the packet and propose dates for the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[09:18] Maria: Thanks.

(End of recording — remaining minutes were used for quick side chat about calendar times)

Redwood to share SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, pen test summary, KMS/BYOK details, audit log retention/immutability options, and data deletion SLA. Next step: schedule SE-led technical deep dive and provide benchmark inputs.
